answer.reason: Gezer has a few defining events: its king was struck down helping Lachish, Pharaoh burned it, and Solomon built it.

clauses.english: saw its king Horam struck down by Joshua when he came to help Lachish
clauses.quote: Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua smote him and his people

clauses.english: was taken and burnt with fire by Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave it to his daughter, Solomon's wife
clauses.quote: Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it with fire

doubts: The spelling Gazer in 2SA 5:25 and 1CH 14:16 marks the end of David's pursuit of the Philistines; left out as it is only a boundary of a route and the summary already cites it.
JOS 10:33 is trimmed in the first clause to the king's defeat; the second clause's 'saw its king' wording is kept short.
